questions.q: What is St. Catherine's help-desk lead's explicit requirement for the new unified Service Desk?
options: That the platform preserve the detailed, multi-tier categorization their reporting and staffing decisions already depend on
That their hospital system be given its own separate ServiceNow instance
That all formal change control be removed from the new platform
That their current categories be replaced with Prairie View's simpler process
questions.explain: St. Catherine's is the most IT-mature of the three and is primarily worried about losing reporting precision, not gaining features.

questions.q: What is Lakeshore's help-desk lead most concerned about protecting?
options: Local governance and flexibility — who can change their categories, not just the data itself
A detailed multi-tier category scheme like St. Catherine's
A faster rollout timeline than the other two systems
Removing all local customization in favor of one corporate standard
questions.explain: Lakeshore's strong local-autonomy culture shows up here as a governance requirement: protecting the ability to control their own configuration, not just preserving data fields.

questions.q: Why does Prairie View's help-desk lead weigh the rollout process and timeline as heavily as any technical requirement?
options: Because a past forced consolidation went badly for Prairie View, making trust in the process itself a real project risk
Because Prairie View already has the most advanced categorization scheme of the three
Because Prairie View has no interest in whether the Service Desk is ever delivered
Because Prairie View's IT staff are the largest of the three systems
questions.explain: Prairie View's history with a badly handled forced consolidation eight years ago makes a visible, trustworthy process a legitimate, explicit requirement here.

questions.q: What is the real structural conflict this lesson identifies across the three interviews?
options: St. Catherine's detailed multi-tier categories, Lakeshore's flatter list, and Prairie View's informal process don't map cleanly onto each other
All three systems already use the exact same ticket categorization scheme
None of the three systems has any help-desk process at all today
The conflict is only about which vendor's ticketing tool to decommission first
questions.explain: The three systems' current categorization approaches are genuinely incompatible, not just differently labeled versions of the same thing.

questions.q: What does this lesson say should happen with a real conflict like the categorization mismatch, at the requirements stage?
options: It should be written into the requirements document as an explicit, unresolved open conflict for a deliberate scoping decision later
It should be resolved immediately by adopting whichever system's scheme is easiest to configure
It should be left out of the requirements document entirely
It should be resolved by giving each system a separate ServiceNow instance
questions.explain: An honest open-conflicts section is the point of a real requirements document — it hands Lesson 14's scoping work a deliberate decision to make, not a silently pre-made one.
